Open it on your phone (or any browser), enter the password, check that the verification code matches, and you are in the same terminal session as your computer. setu means "bridge" in Sanskrit.

New here? Follow the Quick start . Setting setu up for a team? Read Always-on service , Audit logging and MDM and managed policy . Want to know what protects you? See the Security model .
setu is a single static binary. You need it on the machine you share from and on any machine you want to join from a terminal. Joining from a browser needs nothing installed.

go install github.com/dmdhrumilmistry/setu/cmd/setu@latest This needs Go 1.27.2 or newer. The binary lands in $(go env GOPATH)/bin (usually ~/go/bin ); make sure that directory is on your PATH . Check the installation: setu version setu version prints the version, the commit it was built from and your platform, for example setu v0.0.0-... (1a2b3c4d5e6f 2026-10-14T12:00:00Z) linux/amd64 .

Tagged releases publish binaries for Linux, macOS and Windows (amd64 and arm64) on the releases page , named setu-<version>-<os>-<arch> ( .exe on Windows), together with a SHA256SUMS file. # Linux / macOS example curl -LO https://github.com/dmdhrumilmistry/setu/releases/download/<version>/setu-<version>-linux-amd64 curl -LO ...

git clone https://github.com/dmdhrumilmistry/setu cd setu go build -o setu ./cmd/setu # setu.exe on Windows Cross-compile with GOOS and GOARCH , for example GOOS=windows GOARCH=arm64 CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./cmd/setu .

Windows. Hosting uses the ConPTY pseudo console, so it needs Windows 10 1809 / Server 2019 or newer. With no command, setu shares PowerShell 7 ( pwsh ), then Windows PowerShell, then cmd.exe . npm shims such as claude.cmd work. The shared command runs in a job object, so it cannot outlive setu. macOS and Linux. With no command, setu shares $SHELL (or /bin/sh ). Networks. setu needs outbound ...

This takes about two minutes: share a terminal from your computer and open it on your phone.

On the computer you want to share from: setu share --password setu asks you to choose a session password, then prints the invite: setu v1.0.0 - sharing /bin/bash peer-to-peer CONTROL link - anyone holding it can type into this terminal. Keep it secret: browser: https://dmdhrumilmistry.github.io/setu/#k=Pqv4WrBl... terminal: setu join 'k=Pqv4WrBl...' [QR code] Security: password required, max 2 ...

Scan the QR code with your phone's camera (or send yourself the browser link over a channel you trust) and open it. Enter the session password. Compare the verification code on your phone with the one the host terminal prints for the new client. They must be the same. Type. On a phone, use the key bar for Esc, Tab, Ctrl, arrows and ^C, and the pencil button to compose longer text.
setu join 'k=Pqv4WrBl...' Quote the link: it contains characters your shell would otherwise interpret. Type <Enter> ~ . to detach.

On the host, type <Enter> ~ . (Enter, then tilde, then period), or press Ctrl+C in a headless share. When the shared program exits, the share ends too. Treat the link like a password. Anyone with a control link (and the password, if you set one) gets a shell on your machine. Do not paste links into chats, issue trackers or AI prompts.

Sharing a terminal : view-only links, single-use links, expiry, approvals and background shares. Claude Code from your phone : a safe setup for agents. Always-on service : a link that keeps working after reboots.
setu share runs a command in a pseudo terminal and lets other devices join it. Everything after -- is the command; without one, setu shares your shell. setu share [flags] [--] [command [args...]]

setu share --password -- claude setu prompts for a password (8 characters or more). Joiners must enter it. The password never crosses the network: the host sends a challenge and the joiner answers with a proof bound to that exact encrypted connection. After 5 wrong passwords the share refuses new joiners for 10 minutes, and after 20 the invite is disabled for good. For scripts, set SETU_PASSWORD ...

setu share --view-link -- htop Prints a second, independent link whose holders can watch but not type. The role is decided by which link was used, never by anything the client claims. View-only clients' keystrokes and resizes are dropped.

Flag Effect --once The invite stops working after the first successful join. --expire 30m Stop accepting new joiners after this long. Connected clients stay connected. --max-clients 1 At most this many connected clients (default 2). --approve Ask y/N on the host terminal for every joiner, showing their verification code. Combine them for one-off help sessions: setu share --password --once ...

s: Verify who you are talking to
t: When a client connects, the host terminal prints a line such as: [setu] client #1 connected via nostr, role=control: shared-control-link (client #1 from 203.0.113.7:51234, device alice-laptop (linux/amd64, setu-cli), verification code 058 186) The joiner sees the same 6-digit verification code. The code is derived from both ends' DTLS certificates: if the codes differ, someone is intercepting the ...

setu share -d --password -- claude -d (or --background ) prints the links and QR code and gives you your prompt back. The share keeps running after you close the terminal. setu ps # list background shares setu link <id> # show the links and QR code again setu logs <id> # who connected, with verification codes setu stop <id> # end one share setu stop --all # end all of them Each background share ...

Flag Effect --headless Do not attach this terminal; just serve clients (for tmux, nohup or CI). --qr=false Do not print the QR code. --link-file PATH Also write the invite link(s) to PATH with mode 0600. --verbose Log signaling and connection details.

setu share --manual Manual mode sends nothing to nostr relays. setu prints an offer code (and a link containing it). Send it to the joiner, who opens the link or runs setu join <offer-code> and gets an answer code back. Paste the answer code into the host terminal and press Enter. Pasting the answer is itself the approval. Only STUN is used to find a network path.

Peer-to-peer connections need both sides to reach each other. setu uses Google's public STUN servers to discover public addresses. When both sides are behind strict NATs or firewalls that block UDP, add a TURN relay: export SETU_TURN_PASSWORD='...' setu share --turn turn:turn.example.com:3478 --turn-user alice -- claude Flag Effect --stun URL Use these STUN servers instead of Google's ...

By default setu uses four public nostr relays: wss://relay.damus.io , wss://nos.lol , wss://relay.primal.net and wss://nostr.mom . They only carry a few small, encrypted, ephemeral messages per join. To use your own: setu share --relay wss://relay.example.com -- claude Custom relays are embedded in the invite link, so joiners use them too.

The browser client is a static page published from this repository to GitHub Pages. You can host the web/ directory anywhere that serves static files over HTTPS and point links at it: setu share --web-url https://setu.example.com/ -- claude setu share --web-url= -- claude # terminal-only links, no browser URL
Add --audit-endpoint https://collector.example.com:4318 to send an audit log of connections and typed commands to your OpenTelemetry collector. See Audit logging .
See the CLI reference .
You can join a share from any modern browser, including phones, or from a terminal with setu join .

Open the invite link (or scan the QR code). The page: connects to the host through the relays named in the link, asks for the session password if the host set one, shows the verification code : compare it with the code the host terminal prints for your connection, opens the terminal. The secret in the link sits after # , which browsers never send to the web server. The page removes it from the ...

Below the terminal there is a key bar: Key Sends Esc, Tab, Shift+Tab the key Ctrl makes the next key a control key (Ctrl, then r sends Ctrl+R) ^C, ^D interrupt, end of input arrows cursor keys Enter Enter pencil opens a compose box The compose box is for longer text such as prompts. Multi-line text is sent as a single bracketed paste, so programs like Claude Code treat it as one message. "press ...
You can also open the web client directly and paste an invite link, a bare k=... fragment, or a manual-mode offer code into the box on its home screen.

setu join 'https://dmdhrumilmistry.github.io/setu/#k=...' setu join 'k=...' Always quote the link. If the host set a password, setu prompts for it (or reads SETU_PASSWORD ). Type <Enter> ~ . to detach; ~~ sends a literal tilde at the start of a line. Flag Effect --timeout 3m Give up connecting after this long. --relay URL Override the relays in the link. --anonymous Do not send device details ...

If the host used --manual , they send you an offer code or link instead: open the offer link, or run setu join <offer-code> ; send the answer code it prints back to the host over any channel; the host pastes it, and the connection opens.

s: What the host learns about you
t: Like any peer-to-peer connection, the host sees your network address. If the host keeps an audit log , it records: your network origin: the address of the connection, your public address as your router presents it, and (terminal clients only) your local addresses; the verification code and the encryption fingerprint of your connection; device details your client reports: app and version, ...
See Troubleshooting for connections that never open, wrong passwords and mismatched verification codes.
setu was built for this: start Claude Code (or another agent) on your workstation, then follow along and answer its questions from your phone.

cd ~/projects/my-app setu share --password -- claude Scan the QR code, enter the password, check the verification code, and you see Claude Code exactly as it looks on your computer. Use the compose box (pencil key) to write prompts: multi-line text arrives as one paste, so Claude Code treats it as a single message.

s: Keep it running while you are away
t: Run the share in the background so you can close the terminal: setu share -d --password --expire 8h -- claude setu ps # later: is it still running? setu stop <id> # done for the day Or make it permanent with the Always-on service , which restarts Claude Code if it exits and keeps the same link across reboots: setu service add --person me --dir ~/projects/my-app claude -- claude setu service ...

An agent with a shell on your machine is powerful, and a setu link gives that power to whoever holds it. Always set a password for anything that lives longer than a few minutes. Prefer short lifetimes : --expire 8h for ad-hoc shares, --valid-for 168h for service profiles. Use --max-clients 1 so a second device cannot join unnoticed. Check the verification code every time you connect. Run the ...

Lost the link? setu link <id> for background shares, or setu service link <profile> for the service. The web client keeps the terminal size of your phone; the latest control client to resize wins. If your phone sleeps, reopen the link: the replay buffer shows you the last 256 KiB of output.

setu share links last as long as the share. The setu service keeps shares available all the time: it starts at login, serves every enabled profile , restarts the shared program when it exits, and keeps each profile's links the same across reboots.

Profile. A command plus its persistent invite keys and settings, for example " claude in ~/projects/app ". Each profile has a name. Personal key. A link that belongs to one named person. The service knows who connected from which key decrypted their request, so the audit log names them. Revoking one person's key affects nobody else. Shared link. A link anyone can hold; audit records can only say ...

setu service add --person alice --person bob --no-shared-key \ --dir ~/projects/app claude -- claude setu asks for a profile password (12 characters or more), resolves claude to an absolute path, and prints each person's link and QR code once. Send each person only their own link. Flag Default Meaning --person NAME none Create a personal control link for NAME (repeatable). --no-shared-key off No ...

Commands are pinned to absolute paths, so a directory added to PATH later cannot substitute another program. Only one supervisor can serve a state directory at a time. setu can keep an audit trail of every shared session: who connected, from where and on what device, and every command they typed. Records are exported as OpenTelemetry log records over OTLP/HTTP, so they go to any collector and from there to Loki, Elasticsearch, Splunk, Datadog or any other OTLP-capable backend.

For one share: export OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS='Authorization=Bearer%20<ingest-token>' setu share --audit-endpoint https://otel.example.com:4318 --audit-required -- claude For the always-on service : setu service audit --endpoint https://otel.example.com:4318 On managed devices, an MDM policy can force auditing on and users cannot turn it off or redirect it. Flag ( setu share ) Meaning --audit ...

s: How commands are recorded, and the limits
t: setu sees keystrokes, not what the shell finally ran. It rebuilds each line the way a line editor would (backspace, Ctrl+U, Ctrl+W, bracketed paste, Enter) and attributes it to the client that typed it. Lines that used arrow keys, history or tab completion are flagged setu.input.edited=true , because the shell may have run something slightly different. Text typed but never submitted is recorded ...

On Linux and macOS, a line typed while the terminal has echo off (sudo, ssh, other password prompts) is replaced by [REDACTED: typed with terminal echo off] . Windows ConPTY does not expose this state, so there only pattern redaction applies. Known secret formats are redacted: AWS keys, GitHub and Slack tokens, Anthropic and OpenAI keys, JWTs, bearer tokens, password= -style assignments, ...

Records are batched and sent every second through a bounded queue (8192 records; the oldest are dropped if the collector is down for long). The terminal never waits for the network. Because records leave the machine within about a second, someone who later gains control of the host cannot erase what was already exported. Export errors are logged at most once a minute.

Any OTLP/HTTP endpoint works. Here is an example configuration for the OpenTelemetry Collector contrib distribution ( otelcol-contrib ) that accepts setu records over TLS with a bearer token and writes them to a file. Replace the file exporter with your backend's exporter. Adjust and test it for your environment. extensions: bearertokenauth: token: ${env:SETU_INGEST_TOKEN} receivers: otlp: ...

Organizations can manage setu through their MDM (Microsoft Intune, Jamf Pro, Kandji, Mosyle, VaanarSena, Workspace ONE, ...), Group Policy, or configuration management (Ansible, Puppet, Chef, Salt). An administrator deploys a managed policy ; setu enforces it on every device. Users see the policy in force with: setu policy Ready-made templates are in deploy/mdm .

turn off ad-hoc sharing, the background service, or manual mode; require passwords (with a minimum length) and personal keys; cap concurrent clients, share duration and service key lifetime; allow only certain programs, relays and web client URLs; force audit logging to the organization's collector, and add device attributes (such as an asset tag) to every record.

The first source found wins. All of them are writable only by administrators. OS Source Deploy with Windows registry HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\setu the ADMX template (Group Policy, Intune, VaanarSena) or the .reg file Windows %ProgramData%\setu\policy.json , owned by Administrators or SYSTEM a script macOS managed preferences for io.github.dmdhrumilmistry.setu the .mobileconfig profile, installed at ...

Every setting is optional; without a policy setu behaves as unmanaged. Key Type Effect DisableShare bool setu share is refused. DisableService bool setu service cannot add profiles, and a running service stops serving. DisableManual bool setu share --manual is refused, so all signaling uses the allowed relays. RequirePassword bool Every share and profile needs a password; setu share prompts even ...

In Devices > Configuration > Import ADMX , upload setu.admx and en-US/setu.adml . Create an Administrative templates (imported) profile and configure the settings under setu (terminal sharing) . For Macs, upload the .mobileconfig as a custom device-level profile.

Copy setu.admx to \\<domain>\SYSVOL\<domain>\Policies\PolicyDefinitions\ and setu.adml to its en-US folder. The settings appear under Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > setu (terminal sharing) . To test on one machine, import setu-policy.reg as an administrator.

Upload setu.mobileconfig as a custom profile with device-level (System) scope. In Jamf's Application & Custom Settings you can instead set the preference domain to io.github.dmdhrumilmistry.setu and paste the keys from the example policy.

vsctl apply -f deploy/mdm/vaanarsena/setu.yaml The manifest applies the policy on macOS (custom payload), Windows (ADMX ingestion plus OMA-URI settings) and Linux (an onboarding script that installs /etc/setu/policy.json ; it runs once per device, so re-run it after changing the policy).
sudo sh deploy/mdm/linux/install-policy.sh policy.json With Ansible, copy the file to /etc/setu/policy.json with owner: root , group: root and mode: "0644" .

Fail closed. If a policy source exists but is unreadable, malformed, has an unknown key (a typo such as DisableShre must not silently allow sharing), or could have been written by a non-administrator, setu refuses to run rather than ignoring it. Enforced where it runs. setu share checks the policy at start; the service checks profiles when they are created and re-checks every profile every 10 ...

$ setu policy source: /etc/setu/policy.json hash: 7637e6a00b7572df { "DisableManual": true, ... } $ setu share -- htop setu: blocked by your organization's policy (AllowedCommands): "htop" may not be shared (allowed: claude, bash, pwsh) Header values are shown as [hidden] . Every audit record carries setu.policy.hash , so your SIEM can show which policy version applied to each session.
setu gives another device a live shell on your machine , often one running an AI agent with access to your files and credentials. Treat every invite link like an SSH private key.

Layer How Invite secret 256 random bits per share, carried only in the URL fragment ( #k=... ), which browsers never send to the page's web server. The web page removes it from the address bar and history as soon as it loads. Signaling privacy Every relay message is AES-256-GCM encrypted with a key derived (HKDF-SHA256) from the secret. Relays see a random room id, throwaway public keys, message ...

Anyone with a control link (and the password, if set) gets a shell. Do not paste links into chats, issue trackers or AI prompts. Use a password for anything long-lived, and --once or --expire for one-off sharing. The hosted web page is code you trust. Whoever controls the GitHub Pages site could ship JavaScript that leaks secrets. If that matters, self-host web/ , pin a fork, or use setu join ...

s: The browser stays on "connecting" or the join times out
t: The two peers could not reach each other. Make sure the share is still running on the host ( setu ps for background shares). Check that the link is complete. Links copied from some apps get cut at # or & ; scanning the QR code avoids that. Try --verbose on both sides to see which step fails: relays, offer and answer, or the WebRTC connection. If the host logs "no nostr relay reachable", the ...
Same cause as above: no network path. TURN is the fix for strict networks.
The share reached --max-clients , was --once and someone already joined, or it expired ( --expire ), or too many wrong passwords disabled it. Start a new share.

s: "host is temporarily locked after failed logins"
t: Five wrong passwords lock the share for 10 minutes. Twenty disable the invite.

s: The verification codes do not match
t: Disconnect immediately. Different codes mean the two ends are not talking to each other directly: someone is intercepting the connection. Start a new share with a new link and share it over a channel you trust.

For setu share : end the share ( <Enter> ~ . , or setu stop <id> ) and start a new one; the old link dies with it. For the service: setu service rotate <profile> invalidates every link at once, or setu service key remove <profile> <person> revokes one person's.

s: The service does not serve a profile
t: Run setu service status and setu service list , then read the log ( journalctl --user -u setu on Linux, service.log in the state directory on macOS and Windows). Common causes: the profile is disabled or expired (run setu service rotate <profile> ); auditing is configured but the collector is unreachable (the service fails closed until it is back); a managed policy blocks the profile (the log ...
Only one supervisor may serve a state directory. Stop the other one, or use SETU_SERVICE_DIR for a second, independent set of profiles.

s: The service stops when I log out (Linux)
t: systemd user services stop at logout. Run loginctl enable-linger $USER once.

s: claude is not found by the service
t: The service resolves commands to absolute paths when you add a profile. If you installed the tool later or moved it, remove and re-add the profile. On Linux and macOS, reinstall the service ( setu service install ) from a shell whose PATH contains the tool.

--audit-required (or the service default) checks the collector before sharing. Check the URL, the OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS token, and TLS. Plain http:// is refused for remote collectors unless you pass --audit-insecure .
A managed policy forbids that setting. setu policy shows the policy and where it came from; the key in parentheses tells you which rule applied.

s: "managed policy ...: writable by group or others" or "unknown setting"
t: The policy exists but is unsafe or malformed, so setu refuses to run. Ask your administrator to fix it; it must be owned by root (or Administrators) and use only known settings.

Do I need to run a server? No. Relays and STUN are public infrastructure, and you can choose your own or use --manual to need neither. Can the relays or GitHub see my terminal? No. Relays carry only encrypted connection setup messages, and the terminal stream goes directly between the two peers over DTLS. GitHub Pages only serves the static web page; the secret in the link's #fragment is never ...

setu (सेतु, "bridge") shares a local terminal with a browser or another terminal, peer-to-peer over WebRTC, with no server you have to run . Its main job is driving Claude Code and other AI agents on your machine from anywhere, such as your phone.

Goal How No central server WebRTC data channel straight between the peers. Signaling goes over public nostr relays (a decentralised network with many independent operators) or over copy/paste . Google STUN only helps the peers find a network path. Works from a phone Static web client on GitHub Pages , with a QR code, a mobile key bar (Esc, Tab, ⇧Tab, Ctrl, arrows) and a compose box for long ...

Go has pion/webrtc , the most mature WebRTC stack outside browsers, and creack/pty . It also cross-compiles to a single static binary with CGO_ENABLED=0 , and it has HKDF, PBKDF2, AES-GCM and HMAC in its standard library. The Rust options ( webrtc-rs ) are less mature for this use.
